title: Gondwana-derived fossils reveal a hidden biogeographic history of Atypoidea (Araneae: Mygalomorphae)
content:
Abstract
Fossils are essential for understanding the evolutionary history of ancient lineages. Extant members and previously documented fossils of Atypoidea are largely confined to the Holarctic, except for a few southern-living taxa. Here, we describe 2 new fossils from the mid-Cretaceous Kachin amber, which represent the first Atypoidea fossil records from a Gondwana-derived terrane. Our phylogenetic analyses, covering all extant genera and fossil records of this superfamily, show that the 2 new fossils belong to Antrodiaetidae. Moreover, most previously reported atypoid fossils are not placed within the phylogenetic positions originally proposed for them. Divergence time and ancestral range estimations indicate that Atypoidea likely originated in northern Pangea during the Permian and subsequently spread to the Southern Hemisphere at least 3 times. These findings suggest that the ancestor of Antrodiaetidae may have dispersed southward into Gondwana prior to the breakup of Pangea, uncovering a previously hidden historical biogeography of Atypoidea.
